recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future pagination or _count work can clarify separate edge cases if needed, but FHIR-22702 itself is already correctly represented.
issue_request: FHIR-22702 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-I clarification for R5 asking the specification to state that URL parameter order does not drive search processing except for sort ordering: filters are applied first, then sorting, then paging, then _include/_revinclude resources are returned for each page.
initial_application: PR 1282 applied the request in commit 142ad7624ca77d81a9463a6ddbd278f521a109da, which added the order-of-operations paragraph to source/search.html. That commit also addressed FHIR-19523 and FHIR-23809, but the FHIR-22702 wording is separately visible in the patch.
additional_context: source/search.html remains the active authoritative Search page and still contains the requested sequence. source/searchparameter-registry.html is only the search-parameter listing and links back to search.html for search behavior, so it does not need duplicate wording. Later search/count clarifications, including the current _count text that applies only to entry.search.mode = match and excludes included resources and OperationOutcome entries, support rather than contradict the paging-before-includes rule. The origin Zulip thread matches the Jira description, and Confluence searches found no conflicting meeting evidence.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The published commit is an empty audit record because the current specification already implements the final issue decision.
